results.title: Fully Integrated On-FPGA Molecular Dynamics Simulations
results.content: • The first implementation of full MD (RL, LR, and Bonded force with Motion Integration) on a single FPGA, that com-pletely removes the dependency on off-chip devices, thus eliminating the communication overhead of data transfer; • The first analysis of mappings among particles/cells, on-chip memories (BRAMs), on-chip compute units (pipelines) of LR, RL, and bonded forces; • Various microarchitecture contributions related to every as-pect of the system, including exploration of RL particle-pair filtering (on-the-fly neighbor lists), two sets of memory archi-tectures (distributed for RL and LR, and global for Bonded), a scoreboarding mechanism that enables motion update in parallel with the force evaluation, and integrating motion update; • Application-aware optimizations through HDL generator scripts. results.title: Can an FPGA beat a DSP on a performance per cost basis for audio processing? - Quora
results.content: Can an FPGA beat a DSP on a performance per cost basis for audio processing? If there is just a single, unchanging algorithm that needs to be implemented, than yes, an FPGA solution is essentially running the algorithm on hardware, so it's definitely going to be faster than a general purpose DSP chip that can be programmed to run any number of static algorithms, time-varying algorithms, and even algorithms that learn, modify and optimize themselves. results.title: FPGA : Multiply Adder IPCore latency - NI Community
results.content: Home Community Discussion Forums Most Active Software Boards LabVIEW Topic. # LabVIEW. * Float this Topic for Current User. ## FPGA : Multiply Adder IPCore latency. ## FPGA : Multiply Adder IPCore latency. ‎07-19-2016 07:55 AM - edited ‎07-19-2016 07:55 AM. I'm using a set of Xilinx IPCores in my design and have been switching some high throughput add and multiply primitives over to the equivalent DSP-based IPCore MultAdd code and have a question I can't find an answer to on the web. If I set A to unsigned, the Latency is 4 and 3. I thought the DSPs were capable of handling 25x8 Multiplications and 48 bit adds in a single step. ## Re: FPGA : Multiply Adder IPCore latency. ‎07-19-2016 10:42 AM. That would be a weird and unusual way of definining it, but it is consistent with the observation that making A 24 bits reduces the latency. ## Re: FPGA : Multiply Adder IPCore latency. According to datasheet (   ) you get AB = 3 and C = 2 in single DSP slice implementation (page 5). Notice that all the DSP48  specifications say that they have two's complement multipliers - which are signed. If you're using unsigned type, you're actually using one more bit which is normally sign bit (so single DPS is doing fine with 17-bit x17-bit unsigned inputs, or 18-bit signed x 17-bit unsigned). For comparison, DSP48E1 on Virtex-7 and Kintex-7 ( , page 9) and DSP48E on Virtex-5 ( ) have "25 × 18 two’s-complement multiplier". When you switch to unsigned, you're over the DSP multiplying capabilities. As for the DSP usage for unsigned configuration, I'd wager you're using 2 DSPs for multiplication and 1 more for addition. You can try to configure Multiplier and Adder Subtracter cores to see how many resources they use, and their sum should tell you about your Multiply Adder. ## Re: FPGA : Multiply Adder IPCore latency. ‎07-19-2016 04:42 PM. ## Re: FPGA : Multiply Adder IPCore latency. ‎07-20-2016 02:09 AM. Well that would explain it actually, the DSP treating the unsigned version as a 26-bit signed value and ignoring the sign so to speak.
